intent: Move a Questionnaire back to the previous enabled item.
typical_uses: The back action of a questionnaire's navigation row

dont_use_when.situation: An action button outside a questionnaire

invariants.text: `variant` and `size` are passed to the kit Button the component renders by default; when `render` is given it replaces that Button and both are ignored.
It is hidden on the first item. While hidden it carries the native `hidden` and `inert` attributes, `aria-hidden` and tabIndex -1, and `data-hidden` in place of `data-visible`.
Going back never runs validation; the current item's answer stays as it is.

anti_patterns.dont: Hide or remove QuestionnairePrevious yourself on the first item
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mount it always; it hides itself where there is nowhere to go back to

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts Previous has the hidden property on the first item and loses it once the flow advances

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`QuestionnaireNavigationState`: disabled, shortcut, status, visible), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Button.

good.title: A smaller Previous button with its own text

bad.title: Previous mounted only after the first item
bad.why: The button already hides itself on the first item; a hand-written condition repeats state the root owns and goes wrong as soon as the first item is disabled or `items` changes order.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireNavigationState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`QuestionnaireNavigationState`: disabled, shortcut, status, visible), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Button.
